output: ## UX review: signup form Reviewed: the code of the signup form (two fields, "Create account", "Reset", and the script that sends the form). Layout input: none. Main goal: create an account Steps to main goal: 1 (signup form; the next page, "/welcome", is not in the input) Findings: 9 (S1: 3, S2: 2, S3: 3, S4: 1) ### Findings 1. **Signup form, "Create account" control** | S1 Blocker | R-ux-review-1 - Evidence: ".go { color:#111; font-size:16px; cursor:default; }" - Shown absent: The style has no border, fill or underline, and the pointer stays an arrow, so nothing marks it as clickable. - User experiences: The user fills in both fields, sees only plain text below them, does not realise it can be clicked, and never submits. - Recommendation: Make the "Create account" control look and respond like a clickable button, so it is recognisable as the way to submit. 2. **Signup form, failed signup handler** | S1 Blocker | R-ux-review-6 - Evidence: "if (!r.ok) { alert('Error'); signup.reset(); }" - User experiences: The user submits, sees a pop-up that says only "Error", and finds both fields emptied, with no idea what went wrong or what to change. - Recommendation: Show the error next to the field that caused it, say what the user must do next, and keep everything the user typed. 3. **Signup form, "Reset" link** | S1 Blocker | R-ux-review-5 - Evidence: "function clearAll() { signup.reset(); }" - User experiences: The user clicks "Reset" next to the main button, and the email and password vanish at once with no way back. - Recommendation: Ask for confirmation or offer undo before the form is cleared, or drop the clearing control, since a signup form gains little from it. 4. **Signup form, "Create account" request** | S2 Major | R-ux-review-2 - Evidence: "const r = await fetch('/api/signup', { method:'POST', body:new FormData(signup) });" - Shown absent: send() shows no loading or progress state while the request runs, and no message if the request itself fails. - User experiences: The user clicks "Create account", sees nothing change while the request runs, and clicks again, possibly sending the signup twice. - Recommendation: Show a visible waiting state as soon as the user submits, and stop further submits until the response arrives. 5. **Signup form, "Create account" and "Reset"** | S2 Major | R-ux-review-9 - Evidence: "margin-left:2px" - User experiences: The user aims at "Create account", the pointer lands on the neighbouring "Reset" link, and the typed details are wiped. - Recommendation: Separate the destructive "Reset" link from the submit control by a clear gap, in its own visible group. 6. **Signup form, email and password fields, "Create account", "Reset"** | S3 Minor | R-ux-review-8 - Evidence: "#signup input { height:28px; }" - User experiences: The user has to aim carefully at 28 px fields and at text-sized controls, especially on a phone, and mis-taps cost time. - Recommendation: Make every field and clickable control at least 44 by 44 px, including any padding around the text. 7. **Signup form, email and password fields** | S3 Minor | R-ux-review-12 - Evidence: "placeholder="Password"" - User experiences: The user starts typing, the hint text disappears, and later cannot tell which field is which without deleting what they typed. - Recommendation: Keep a visible label on each field that stays in view while the user types, instead of using placeholder text as the only label. 8. **Signup form, "Reset" link** | S3 Minor | R-ux-review-12 - Evidence: "Reset" - User experiences: The user sees link-style text and expects it to go to another place, but it silently empties the form instead. - Recommendation: Give the clearing action the look of a button rather than a link, because link-style text must only navigate. 9. **Signup form, email and password fields** | S4 Note | R-ux-review-12 - Evidence: "" - Shown absent: Neither field carries any mark saying that it is required. - User experiences: The user cannot tell before submitting whether both fields are needed. - Recommendation: Mark the required fields before the user submits. ### Not reviewed - Contrast, focus styles, spacing and type scales: a visual polish pass. - Semantics, ARIA and screen-reader output: an accessibility audit. - Wording of labels and messages: a copy edit. ### Open questions - Password field: does the server require a minimum length or other format? The input does not state it, so it is unknown whether the rule is shown before submit. - "/api/signup" response: how long does it take, and what does it return for errors? The server is not in the input. - Email and password fields, "Create account", "Reset": what are the widths and the padding? Only the 28 px field height is given. - "/welcome": does it confirm that the account was created? - Page shape (first screen, page length, number of controls per view): no measurement sheet or screenshot description was given. ### Severity scale - S1 Blocker: the user cannot complete the main goal, or loses data or money. - S2 Major: the user completes the main goal only after a wrong action, an error or a second attempt. - S3 Minor: the user completes the main goal at the first attempt, but more slowly. - S4 Note: the result and the speed do not change; the place departs from the rule.
